title: Replace a Halogen Front Fog Lamp Bulb
introduction:
The halogen fog-lamp bulb comes out from behind the lamp through the front wheel opening. The bulb itself uses a twist-lock fitting; the wheel and inner liner are the backstage door that makes it reachable. I separate those jobs so the small bulb does not distract from the important lifting and wheel-refitting work around it.

Confirm the lamp type first: this procedure covers halogen bulbs. LED fog lamps are serviced as an assembly. The linked lifting and wheel procedures form part of this repair, including the wheel’s final tightening and later retightening.

requirements.category: Prevent an unexpected start and protect yourself

items.name: Remote start and key
items.detail:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the vehicle safely parked, the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Complete remote-start disabling first, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If the menu needs ignition ON, keep a valid key inside and the engine OFF: from ignition OFF, release the pedals and press the start button once; if already ON, leave it ON rather than pressing again.

For an automatic, establish engine-off ignition ON in the same way if it is not already ON, then hold the service brake and select Neutral in the ground-level cabin. With the parking brake and chocks maintaining restraint, release the brake pedal and press the button once to switch ignition OFF. For a manual, switch ignition OFF if it is ON, then select Neutral with the engine OFF while maintaining those restraints. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before hands-on service. Keep the parking brake applied throughout the job.

The ignition controls follow the Ford Mustang owner manual; service precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189). Switch the lighting control to Off before working on the bulb. A remote or accidental engine start during service can cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use this protection can cause serious personal injury. Before using the specified wheel-refitting material, consult its material safety information sheet; improper use can also cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Vehicle position and capacity
items.detail: Keep the parking brake applied and restrain wheels remaining on the ground while positioning the vehicle. The Wheel and Tire procedure requires the vehicle in NEUTRAL when positioning it on the hoist. Verify that hoist capacity covers the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Position the lift arms at the locations in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are off the ground. Incorrect arm placement or drive wheels contacting the ground can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Find the marked lifting locations
items.detail: Locate the triangles stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame. The reference drawing places the lifting locations along the side sills behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious personal injury. Use the linked drawing to confirm the exact locations before lifting.

items.name: Avoid contact damage
items.detail: Keep hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage. On a two-column hoist, ensure the forks clear suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets if equipped; also avoid damaging the axle or rear cover. If using drive-on equipment, check for underbody interference before driving onto it.

items.name: Do not substitute the emergency jack
items.detail: The vehicle’s supplied jack is only for emergency replacement of a deflated tire; using it for this repair can damage the vehicle. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack: it can lower unexpectedly and cause serious personal injury. Floor stands are required for jack-supported work. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because bumper-cover damage will occur.

items.name: Cracked wheel
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle. A cracked wheel can be dangerous, and failing to take this precaution can cause serious personal injury. See [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Equipment and material
items.detail: Have equipment suitable for the specified wheel-nut final tightening and Motorcraft® High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant / XL-2, specified in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Apply it only to the wheel-pilot/hub-pilot interface as explained below. The tire remains mounted on its wheel for this job; tire-changing and balancing operations are outside this repair.

items.name: Brake dust precaution
items.detail: Do not breathe friction dust or blow it from brake components with compressed air. Use approved dust-control techniques and avoid dispersing residue; it can present serious respiratory and other health hazards. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). Control dust before disturbing dusty components or beginning mounting-face preparation.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

requirements.category: Lowering and returning to the parked state

items.name: Keep restraint continuous
items.detail: After the wheels are seated and their nuts initially finger tight, keep the parking brake applied while lowering. Restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground, then perform the final wheel-nut tightening below with the car resting on its tires.

items.name: Restore the grounded parked state
items.detail: After tightening, with the vehicle fully grounded, chocked and the parking brake still applied, restore its parked gear. For an automatic, enter the ground-level cabin with the valid key, release the pedals and press the button once from known ignition OFF for engine-off ON. Hold the service brake, select Park, then release the brake and press the button once for OFF. For a manual, keep the engine and ignition OFF and select a parked gear. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before leaving.

edits.text: NOTE: Use this procedure only for halogen fog-lamp bulbs. LED fog lamps are serviced as an assembly.
edits.why: Identify the fitted lamp before opening up the wheel arch. The removable halogen bulb and an LED lamp assembly have different service paths.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps for installation details as well; refitting information may appear alongside removal instructions.
edits.why: The repair includes restoring the wheel and liner, so completion involves more than locking the replacement bulb into the lamp.

edits.text:
Raise the vehicle on a hoist after completing the lifting preparation above.
Refer to: [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The hoist provides access for front-wheel removal. Confirm the stamped lifting marks and adapter clearance before the vehicle leaves the ground.

edits.text:
Remove the front wheels and tires as complete assemblies.
Refer to: [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) (204-04A Wheels and Tires, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: With the vehicle positioned on the hoist as required, remove the wheel nuts and take off the wheel-and-tire assemblies. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Removing the wheels opens access to the inner fender liners.

edits.text: Remove the push pins along the forward edge of the inner fender liner, then move the liner aside to expose the rear of the fog lamp.
edits.why: The drawing highlights the liner attachments at the front of the wheel opening. Only moving the liner aside is required; the lamp is reached from behind it.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector from the back of the front fog-lamp bulb.
edits.why: The connector plugs into the bulb base on the rear of the lower lamp. Freeing it first allows the bulb to turn without twisting the attached wiring.

edits.text: Viewed from behind the fog lamp, turn the bulb counterclockwise to release its locking tabs, then withdraw the front fog-lamp bulb from the housing.
edits.why: The rear-view drawing shows the turning movement at the bulb base. This is a twist-lock fitting, so the release comes from rotating the base before withdrawing it.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence to install the bulb. Insert it into the fog-lamp housing and turn it clockwise to lock it, reconnect the electrical connector, return the inner fender liner to position and reinstall its push pins. Refit the front wheels and tires using the linked Wheel and Tire procedure, then lower the vehicle for final wheel-nut tightening.
edits.why: Apply the brake-dust controls in preparation before disturbing dusty components or cleaning mating faces; dust control and mating-face preparation are separate operations. Before mounting each wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from both the wheel mounting face and the mating hub, brake-disc or brake-drum face. Secure any rotor-to-hub fasteners so they cannot interfere with those faces. Otherwise, wheel nuts can loosen and the wheel can come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death. Apply a thin coat of the specified anti-seize only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot—the centering interface around the wheel’s middle hole. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces to prevent component damage. Position the wheel and initially install the nuts finger tight. With the vehicle resting on its tires and the stud and nut threads clean and dry, tighten in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). The linked drawing shows the alternating path across the hub; tightening around the circle can produce excessive brake-disc runout and accelerate roughness, shudder and vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi): wheels can loosen after initial tightening, with a risk of serious injury to occupants. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). I finish by accounting for the locked bulb, reconnected plug, restored liner attachments and completed wheel tightening. After all refitting and final wheel tightening, complete the grounded parked-state steps above. For an ordinary fog-lamp operation check, keep the parking brake applied, wheels restrained and parked gear selected, with the engine stopped. Bring the valid key inside; from confirmed ignition OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal for engine-off ON. Select the headlamp position on the main lighting control. Keep high beams OFF; if they are on, pull the steering-column lighting lever toward you to switch them off. Use the front fog-lamp button in the lighting-control panel: if the fog lamps are OFF, press it to turn them on; if already ON, leave them ON. Observe that the serviced lamp illuminates. Press the fog-lamp button to turn the lamps off, then return the main lighting control to Off. From that known ignition ON state, press and release START/STOP without pressing a pedal to return OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key. Leave the parking brake applied and parked gear selected. This is an ordinary operation check, not aim adjustment or fault isolation; if the lamp does not respond normally, stop and use the matching lighting diagnosis before further dismantling. See the [matching owner manual, Lighting and Starting](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for the fitted controls.
